comment:
* Reads and decodes protocol message fields.
 *
 * This class contains two kinds of methods:  methods that read specific
 * protocol message constructs and field types (e.g. {@link #readTag()} and
 * {@link #readInt32()}) and methods that read low-level values (e.g.
 * {@link #readRawVarint32()} and {@link #readRawBytes}).  If you are reading
 * encoded protocol messages, you should use the former methods, but if you are
 * reading some other format of your own design, use the latter.
 *
 * @author kenton@google.com Kenton Varda

variables.name: currentLimit
variables.comment: The absolute position of the end of the current message.

methods.name: public static CodedInputByteBufferNano newInstance(final byte[] buf)
methods.comment: * Create a new CodedInputStream wrapping the given byte array.

methods.name: public static CodedInputByteBufferNano newInstance(final byte[] buf, final int off, final int len)
methods.comment: * Create a new CodedInputStream wrapping the given byte array slice.

methods.name: public int readTag() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Attempt to read a field tag, returning zero if we have reached EOF.
   * Protocol message parsers use this to read tags, since a protocol message
   * may legally end wherever a tag occurs, and zero is not a valid tag number.

methods.name: public void checkLastTagWas(final int value) throws InvalidProtocolBufferNanoException
methods.comment:
* Verifies that the last call to readTag() returned the given tag value.
   * This is used to verify that a nested group ended with the correct
   * end tag.
   *
   * @throws InvalidProtocolBufferNanoException {@code value} does not match the
   *                                        last tag.

methods.name: public boolean skipField(final int tag) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Reads and discards a single field, given its tag value.
   *
   * @return {@code false} if the tag is an endgroup tag, in which case
   *         nothing is skipped.  Otherwise, returns {@code true}.

methods.name: public void skipMessage() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Reads and discards an entire message.  This will read either until EOF
   * or until an endgroup tag, whichever comes first.

methods.name: public static int decodeZigZag32(final int n)
methods.comment:
* Decode a ZigZag-encoded 32-bit value.  ZigZag encodes signed integers
   * into values that can be efficiently encoded with varint.  (Otherwise,
   * negative values must be sign-extended to 64 bits to be varint encoded,
   * thus always taking 10 bytes on the wire.)
   *
   * @param n An unsigned 32-bit integer, stored in a signed int because
   *          Java has no explicit unsigned support.
   * @return A signed 32-bit integer.

methods.name: public static long decodeZigZag64(final long n)
methods.comment:
* Decode a ZigZag-encoded 64-bit value.  ZigZag encodes signed integers
   * into values that can be efficiently encoded with varint.  (Otherwise,
   * negative values must be sign-extended to 64 bits to be varint encoded,
   * thus always taking 10 bytes on the wire.)
   *
   * @param n An unsigned 64-bit integer, stored in a signed int because
   *          Java has no explicit unsigned support.
   * @return A signed 64-bit integer.

methods.name: public int setRecursionLimit(final int limit)
methods.comment:
* Set the maximum message recursion depth.  In order to prevent malicious
   * messages from causing stack overflows, {@code CodedInputStream} limits
   * how deeply messages may be nested.  The default limit is 64.
   *
   * @return the old limit.

methods.name: public int setSizeLimit(final int limit)
methods.comment:
* Set the maximum message size. In order to prevent malicious * messages from exhausting memory or causing integer overflows, * {@code CodedInputStream} limits how large a message may be. * The default limit is 64MB. You should set this limit as small * as you can without harming your app's functionality. Note that * size limits only apply when reading from an {@code InputStream}, not * when constructed around a raw byte array. *

* If you want to read several messages from a single CodedInputStream, you * could call {@link #resetSizeCounter()} after each one to avoid hitting the * size limit. * * @return the old limit.

methods.name: public void resetSizeCounter()
methods.comment: * Resets the current size counter to zero (see {@link #setSizeLimit(int)}).

methods.name: public int pushLimit(int byteLimit) throws InvalidProtocolBufferNanoException
methods.comment:
* Sets {@code currentLimit} to (current position) + {@code byteLimit}.  This
   * is called when descending into a length-delimited embedded message.
   *
   * @return the old limit.

methods.name: public void popLimit(final int oldLimit)
methods.comment:
* Discards the current limit, returning to the previous limit.
   *
   * @param oldLimit The old limit, as returned by {@code pushLimit}.

methods.name: public int getBytesUntilLimit()
methods.comment:
* Returns the number of bytes to be read before the current limit.
   * If no limit is set, returns -1.

methods.name: public boolean isAtEnd()
methods.comment:
* Returns true if the stream has reached the end of the input.  This is the
   * case if either the end of the underlying input source has been reached or
   * if the stream has reached a limit created using {@link #pushLimit(int)}.

methods.name: public int getPosition()
methods.comment: * Get current position in buffer relative to beginning offset.

methods.name: public byte[] getData(int offset, int length)
methods.comment:
* Retrieves a subset of data in the buffer. The returned array is not backed by the original
   * buffer array.
   *
   * @param offset the position (relative to the buffer start position) to start at.
   * @param length the number of bytes to retrieve.

methods.name: public void rewindToPosition(int position)
methods.comment: * Rewind to previous position. Cannot go forward.

methods.name: public byte readRawByte() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Read one byte from the input.
   *
   * @throws InvalidProtocolBufferNanoException The end of the stream or the current
   *                                        limit was reached.

methods.name: public byte[] readRawBytes(final int size) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Read a fixed size of bytes from the input.
   *
   * @throws InvalidProtocolBufferNanoException The end of the stream or the current
   *                                        limit was reached.

methods.name: public void skipRawBytes(final int size) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Reads and discards {@code size} bytes.
   *
   * @throws InvalidProtocolBufferNanoException The end of the stream or the current
   *                                        limit was reached.

methods.name: Object readPrimitiveField(int type) throws IOException
methods.comment: Read a primitive type.
